search-mode.summary: Where the search lives: a row under the header, or a panel opened from a magnifier in the header.

search-label.summary: Accessible name and tooltip of the magnifier that opens the search panel.

search-shortcut.summary: The key that opens the search from anywhere on the page; empty turns it off.

search-hint.summary: A short line shown under an empty query, when the host has one.

search-keys-hint.summary: The line of key hints at the bottom of the search panel.

search-title.summary: Heading shown above the search field in the navigation panel.

recent-results.x-summary: what the search panel offers before a query, groups of results (was setRecentResults)

current.x-summary: the row the page is on, by its key: it is marked current and its root's column follows it; empty: the row whose address the page is at (stand 24 A1)
current.summary: The row the page is on, by its key; empty: the row whose address the page is at.

source.x-summary: where the entries come from: items (the setting and the element's children) or port (simai.admin-navigation-port, which the host connects); with port the menu is its navigation skeleton until the host answers, never the empty items menu (first paint, standard 1.3.9 §5.4)
source.summary: Where the entries come from: items (the setting and the children) or port (simai.admin-navigation-port, connected by the host). With port the menu is its navigation skeleton until the host answers.

expected-columns.x-summary: how many columns the navigation skeleton draws on a wide screen before the host answers (source port): 1 where the page's row has no open root (a dashboard), 2 where it has; the server knows which. The shape of the first paint, never a limit: the answered menu takes the columns its rows need
expected-columns.summary: How many columns the navigation skeleton draws on a wide screen before the host answers: 1 where the page's row has no open root (a dashboard), 2 where it has. The server knows which; with the right number the menu is as wide before the answer as after it. Never a limit: the answered menu takes the columns its rows need.

first-answer.x-shape: the host's first answer printed with the page, the applied data of navigation.load (revision, echo, site, current, items, favourites, profiles, rights, person, notifications, and context: the object menu of this page), optionally with capabilities (the port's, known before the port). A server that has the menu prints it in the menu's data-sf-settings island; with source port the menu draws it at once, without a skeleton and without a port, and the port's answer to navigation.load replaces it. Taken once
first-answer.summary: The host's first navigation.load answer printed with the page (the data-sf-settings island). With source port the menu is drawn from it at once, with no skeleton; the port answers behind it.

open.x-summary: whether the menu is shown where a page folds it away (narrower than 48rem): written by the page that opens it from its own button, reflected as data-open; not written: the menu shows as it always has (stand 24 A1)
open.summary: Written by a page that opens the menu from its own button: on a narrow screen the menu is folded away while false (data-open). Not written: no change.

favourite.x-summary: whether the current row is among the person's favourites, as the host last answered; false without a port or a current row (stand 24 A1)

compact-change.summary: Notify the host shell about width mode.

query.x-summary: a query is asked for: the menu's own search (kind menu; was sf-admin-menu-search), a site (sites.search) or the admin search (search.query)
query.summary: a query: kind menu (the items menu), site or search (vocabulary 1.1.5).

settings-mode-change.summary: Request state for another settings level.

settings-refresh.summary: Request fresh backend state after a conflict.

settings-save.summary: Request persistence of the current delta.

reset.x-summary: vocabulary reset: the settings level (kind settings; was sf-admin-menu-settings-reset) or a view (view.reset)
reset.summary: kind settings (the items menu) or view (vocabulary 1.1.5).

navigate.x-summary: the host answered item.open, search.choose or session.sign-out applied: the page goes to href (region: the menu goes there itself)
navigate.summary: The host answered item.open applied: the page belongs to this row now. For a host that navigates in its own router rather than through the address it answered with.

refresh.summary: navigation.load / notifications.load asked of the host (vocabulary 1.1.5).

open.summary: item.open, site.switch, view.profile or search.choose asked (vocabulary 1.1.5).

apply-settings-result.summary: Commit a successful external save response.

apply-settings-error.summary: Keep the draft and expose error or conflict state.

toggle-menu-settings.summary: Enter or leave the settings editor.

refresh.x-summary: read the menu again from the host (navigation.load); the items menu has nothing to read
refresh.summary: Read the navigation menu again from its host, after something outside the menu changed what it shows (a star in the page header). No effect on the items menu.

x-returns.description: A promise that settles when the host has answered.

set-search-results.x-summary: the host's answer to query {kind: menu, request-id}; an older request-id is refused
set-search-results.summary: The host answers one search request with its own groups of results. An answer to a query the person has moved on from is dropped.

x-returns.description: Whether the answer was for the current query and was shown.

toggle.x-summary: add the row id to the person's favourites (on) or take it out (favourite.toggle); the items menu has no favourites and refuses (stand 24 A1)
toggle.summary: Add a row to the person's favourites or take it out (favourite.toggle). The items menu refuses.

x-returns.description: A promise of the outcome: applied, refused or unavailable.

shape (§7): a leaf. The report counts context-menu, dropdown, empty-state, inputs, profile-picker, resizer and sortable as placed parts; each is drawn by the menu's own templates as a control of the menu's own state (a row's menu, the site switcher, the width handle, the edit-mode lists), wired privately, and talks to the host only through the menu's one port. No rule runs between two of them and no key would have two writers, so keys, roles and rules would restate what the controller does (the smaller mechanism). The navigation shell composes the free menu's parts by markup, not by roles.

alias-conflict: vocabulary 1.1.5 §5.1 decides sf-admin-menu-intent: one name per verb, split by detail.intent -- neither the alias table's planned sf-admin-menu nor the conversion's sf-admin-menu-request.

events (vocabulary §5): each port intent is a verb with a kind -- navigation.load refresh; item.open, site.switch, view.profile and search.choose open (kind item, site, view, search); favourite.toggle toggle; preference.* and view.save save; sites.search and search.query query; view.create create; view.rename rename; view.delete delete {ids}; view.reset reset; session.sign-out the own verb sign-out (its word is lang events.sign-out.label). The detail keeps the port's intent and payload, so a 1.0 listener loses nothing.
own-verb-words: search became the vocabulary's query (kind menu); request is not an event (the conversion read it from the old alias plan); sign-out is the one own verb.
setter (§4.4): setRecentResults becomes the setting recent-results; setCompact stays a method of the class (compact is a value a person changes; compact-change reports it, as 1.0 did).

persistence (§7.5): local (localStorage, the key per identity) or external (the host saves; settings-save, settings-refresh, settings-reset carry the base revision); unchanged, and named by persistence-mode.

port (§4.9): simai.admin-navigation-port; connect-port {port} is the base action (setHostPort its alias). sf-host-port-request is still sent until 2026-12-01 for the pages that answer it (ui-admin navigation.ts).
item-shape: recent-results names its groups' fields with `of`; the items menu's own item contract stays in docs.
existing-aliases: none shipped; every rename is in aliases.json with its dates.
words (§11): lang/en.json and lang/ru.json are the one source; js/words.js makes the navigation's, the settings menu's and the counter's dictionaries from them by the keys they always used.
template: templates.default names the Lit templates in JavaScript, the migration form §5.2 allows.

skeleton (§5.4): the menu draws its own loading row while the port answers navigation.load; its first paint is the static snapshot (static/default/<example>.html); with a navigation port the loading row is part of it.
actions: declared with their 1.0 returns (x-outcomes applied). Their outcome objects (§4.4) come with the major at the aliases' end, with the callers in ui-admin -- a leftover of this migration.

examples: examples.json from studio.fixture.json and studio.scenario.json plus the search panel and the navigation shell over a port; probe.json drives the per-verb events through a port, the old intent name, the settings reset and the menu search (gate 16, gate 20).
css-variables: five public variables the navigation shell reads with the role tokens as fallback; the items menu's look is the free admin-menu class's, whose variables are internal.
side-effects: portal (the context menu is drawn in #sf-admin-menu-portal at the end of body).

version 1.3.1: the first paint is retaken on ui-source c020caa: no held copy of the JSON island, no icon-font state, closed surfaces printed closed, no size the code measured; an example may declare a fake host port for gate 24's phase 3.

version 1.4.0: source (items | port): a menu whose entries come from the navigation port is its navigation skeleton -- six rows in the real row markup, both columns on a wide screen and one on a phone by the stylesheet -- from the first paint until the host answers, never the empty items menu; the menu fills its region and its rows scroll inside, so its box holds when the host answers (gate 24 phase 3).

version 1.6.4: the navigation's standard menu (sf-context-menu) and the edit mode's sf-dropdown are asked for through SF.Loader.ensure (core.runtime 1.19.0), not ensurePlugin/ensureSmartElementLoaded and a race of whenDefined against 3 s of its own (reuse audit 2026-11-02, finding 4); without the menu it still falls back as before. Needs core.runtime >= 1.19.0.

version 1.6.5: the ⌘K palette is a modal layer of the one document layer stack (core layer-stack.js, core.runtime 1.19.0; reuse audit 2026-11-02, findings 1 and 2). Escape, Tab and a press on the dimmed page are the stack's while it is the top layer (its own Escape in capture, its scrim's pointerdown and a document pointerdown listener that did nothing are gone); Tab stays inside it with the stack's focus list (focusablesIn), the page does not scroll under it (the stack's page lock, the scrollbar's gap kept), focus goes back to what opened it by the stack's rule, and it is drawn at the stack's height instead of z-index 1000, so it stands over a drawer or a modal it is opened from. Its scrim is the shared one (--sf-scrim-color at --sf-scrim-opacity), not sf-drawer's overlay variables: black at 60 as before; a page that set --sf-drawer-overlay-* on the root no longer tints the palette with them. Needs core.runtime >= 1.19.0.

version 1.6.6: the Framework elements it draws, finds and listens to are named by their new tags (Smart component naming of 2026-11-02, sf-[set]-<block>): the navigation menu and the row menus are sf-menu-context, the icon buttons sf-button-icon. The rule relations and the registry ids follow (cl-<new>, smart.<new>; the package reference pro.package.json of the pair). The former tags stay dated aliases of the Framework until 2027-01-01; public CSS variables and classes keep their names. No visible change. Needs the SIMAI Framework pair with the tag renames (core.runtime 1.21.0).
version 1.6.7: the edit panel imports its icon choices from src/smart/view-properties (rename plan R2 moved the folder); a package build failed on the former path.

version 1.6.8: the row glyph chooser takes SIMAI Framework's choice list (core/js/icon-choices.js, core.runtime 1.25.0; duplication audit 2026-11-03 A-1) instead of importing sf-view-properties' file. Behaviour unchanged.

version 1.7.0 (owner 2026-11-05, after the Larena Panel UX audit; Larena request msg-955aa941487545d68f4a): never more than two menus on screen, and the second column is about where the person is. It shows the page's object menu (navigation.context: title, subtitle, status, back, groups of link rows, current), else the root that holds the page's row, else nothing -- never a root left open on another page (the per-site openRoots memory is gone). A root clicked in the first column is shown until a page is opened; then the column follows the page again. Whether the column is open is the person's one choice on every page and site (SF.Preferences sf-admin-menu/main `second`; a person who had closed it everywhere under openRoots finds it closed), which keeps the 2026-10-13 rule that the menu does not jump open or closed; a closed column with something to show gets a «Показать колонку» button beside the fold. navigation.load carries the page's address as `page` (path and query) and is asked again after a region swap, whose answer replaces or removes the object menu. The object menu's rows are ordinary links: no port intent, no favourite, not in the edit mode; a plain click goes by region when the shell has it and tells `navigate` {id, key, href, region}. On a phone it is the screen the menu opens on, with its back link at the top. New setting first-answer: the first navigation.load answer printed in the data-sf-settings island, drawn at once without a skeleton or a port. Port fields `page` (payload) and `context` (data) are simai.admin-navigation-port 1.1.0 (ui-source), which the menu declares; it still takes a 1.0.0 host, which sends no `context` and ignores `page`. A long row name takes a second line instead of an ellipsis, in both columns and in the object menu (Larena Panel audit, 2026-11-05: «Программы и обновления»): the row grows by one text line, its glyph, chevron and badge stay on the middle of the first line, and a one-line row keeps its height.

version 1.7.1 (Larena Panel UX audit IA-07, Larena request msg-122087e94d724e0990d0): the second column's caption «Общее для всех сайтов» (all-sites) under a section of the install level shows only when the menu offers the site switch (capabilities include site-switch); a host without it has no other site to share with, and the caption is not drawn at all. A section of the site level keeps the current site's name as its caption.

version 1.7.2 (2026-11-07): a patch (a look). A menu row's counter (the class counter and the dot-case sf-badge) and a row's badge draws with sf-badge tight: Framework sf-badge 1.3.0 (component.badges 1.2.0) widens a badge's default side room to --sf-space-1/2 (owner decision, docs review R020), and this is a dense place, so it keeps the size's own narrow room. On a Framework before 1.3.0 the attribute and class do nothing. Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

version 1.7.3: a patch. The settings menu of the items path is a surface of the document's one layer stack (holdOpenSurfaceMark, standard 1.3.8 §19; reuse audit 2026-11-02, findings 1 and 3): a press outside and Escape reach it through the stack's one listener, only while it is the top layer, in place of a document click and keydown of its own; a press on its opener is left to the opener's click (it closes the menu as before); Tab still closes it to the opener. It is drawn at the stack's z-index (--sf-z-index-layer and its step) instead of a fixed 10000 that stood above every modal and drawer. Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

version 1.7.4 (2026-11-08): a patch (a look). A row's shortcut is SIMAI Framework's kbd and nothing of the menu's own: navigation.css no longer sets its colour, size or font (owner decision 2026-11-07, docs review R030, rule C04; tools/lint-kbd-styles.mjs), only flex: none for its place in the row. The rows' kbd (a row's shortcut, the search row's ⌘K) carry appearance="plain": glyphs without plates, muted, a step smaller, as a menu row reads; the palette's ↵ sits in its listbox, where the component picks plain itself. Needs component.kbd >= 1.2.0 for the look; on an earlier Framework the key draws in that release's default look. Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

version 1.7.5 (2026-11-09): a patch (no visible change). The settings menu's entries, the navigation editor's buttons and the shell's icon buttons ask for appearance="ghost", the look SIMAI Framework now calls ghost (decision C15, sf-button 1.7.0 and sf-button-icon of the pair ui-d6f01121baca); link is its former name, a dated alias until 2027-01-01, drawn the same. The search field's Esc key keeps its markup and loses the style of its own (.sf-admin-menu-search-kbd, removed by component.admin-menu 1.0.1): it reads as the Framework's kbd cap by its place in the field (sf-kbd 1.1.0, R030, C04). Settings, values and events are unchanged.

version 1.7.6 (2026-11-09): a patch (a look, the command palette only), for the SIMAI Framework pair with the shadow places (C20, owner 2026-11-08; core.runtime >= 1.43.0). The palette's dialog is a window over the scrim, so it takes the modal place, as sf-modal 1.1.0 of that pair does: --sf-shadow-modal on --sf-surface-popup (was elevation step 3, which resolves to the overlay shadow). The bottom bar under an open menu is the class component's (component.admin-menu of that pair: a 1px inset hairline in --sf-outline-variant instead of the upward shadow); ui-pro draws no shadow of its own there. Settings, values and events are unchanged.

version 1.7.7 (2026-11-09): a patch (no visible change). The navigation's standard menu reads sf-menu-context's answer to openFor in both forms: true or false (up to 1.12.1) and the outcome object {outcome: applied | refused | unavailable} (1.12.2, SIMAI Framework fix/action-call-defects). A refused open used to read as open with the outcome menu and left the site switcher marked open with no list on screen; it now closes again. openMenu answers a boolean (menuOpened in js/navigation/menu.js). Settings, values and events are unchanged.

version 1.7.8 (2026-11-09): a patch (no visible change). SIMAI Framework ui-cb287da78ab1 (core.runtime 1.45.0, standard §4.4) writes an action's method in the reference as one args object whose schema is the action's `with` fields, not the fields one by one (ui-source 9d2eeb8e, generate-component-files.mjs argumentsOf); smart.manifest.json is regenerated and changes only in methods.*.arguments. applyExternalSettingsState, applySettingsResult, applySettingsError and setSearchResults are the class's own methods with the fields in order; elementFromManifest's positional now gives them the object form too (setSearchResults({requestId, groups}) is the same call); toggle already read both. Settings, values and events are unchanged.

notes: An sf-admin-menu-item takes its glyph from the left-icon attribute; an icon attribute on the item is not read. right-icon is read into the item data but no template draws it.

A navigation node from the host (applyExternalSettingsState, simai.admin-navigation-port) carries the glyph as its icon property, which becomes the item's left icon. That is the host's data field, not an alias of the markup attribute.

integration_examples.event_bridge: Register the generic Smart event bridge for save, reset, mode-change and refresh events.

untrusted_inputs: Treat labels, badges and URLs as untrusted render data

ai_guidance.use_when: Use the complete component for product admin navigation with search, nesting, badges, compact mode or editable preferences.
do_not: Do not rebuild the menu from primitive SF tags
Do not store Larena domain state in localStorage
Do not let the browser decide access or routes

accessibility.focus: Context menus focus their first available native item after rendering. Escape returns to the native opener; Tab/Shift+Tab close and continue from the opener. Outside focus is preserved. If save/cancel removes the opener, abandoned body focus returns to the settings control or another available control in this Admin Menu. Shared portal ownership and stale callbacks are guarded. Popup geometry follows the native opener, including display-contents Smart hosts, LTR/RTL, responsive movement, content, font and viewport changes; --sf-context-menu-viewport-space derives from the spacing scale. Internal scrolling preserves the menu; outside document scrolling dismisses it. Search and nested drill-down layers make inactive panels inert. Opening a nested layer focuses its localized Back control; Back restores the corresponding tree trigger. Compact search focuses the revealed input. Search placement and directional chevrons follow LTR or RTL.

changes: The manifest moves to smart-component-manifest v2: persistence, ownership, security, accessibility and state use the v2 shape, and adapter, artifacts and readiness are declared.
The conformance scenarios left the manifest (v2 keeps scenarios in artifacts) and are documented in docs/docs.md; studio.fixture.json and studio.scenario.json are the declared artifacts.

Follows SIMAI Framework release ui-92b4661762ca (standard 1.3.8 display groups A and B): the Loader relations and the composition name the renamed bundles and registry ids (cl-button, cl-badge, cl-icon, cl-icon-button, cl-input; smart.button, smart.badge, smart.icon, smart.icon-button, smart.input).

The navigation listens to sf-profile-picker-* and sf-resizer-resize, and to sf-context-menu-closed for a menu it opened; the search field takes icon-start and the edit form's cancel button the appearance link. No public attribute, property or event of sf-admin-menu changes.
standard simai.smart-component 1.3.8: the element is made from component.json; dated aliases in aliases.json
The standard menu and sf-dropdown are asked for through SF.Loader.ensure; needs core.runtime >= 1.19.0. Nothing to change for a host on a pair from core.runtime 1.19.0 on.

The ⌘K palette joins the layer stack: Escape, Tab, the press on the scrim, the page lock, focus return and its height are the stack's, its scrim the shared --sf-scrim-* (black at 60, as before); needs core.runtime >= 1.19.0. New: the page no longer scrolls under the open palette, and Tab stays inside it. A page that tinted the palette through --sf-drawer-overlay-* sets --sf-scrim-color/--sf-scrim-opacity instead.

Draws and finds the renamed Framework elements by their new tags (the navigation menu and the row menus are sf-menu-context, the icon buttons sf-button-icon); the rule relations name cl-<new>. Needs the SIMAI Framework pair with the tag renames (core.runtime 1.21.0). No visible change. Nothing to change for a host on that pair; a host that writes the former tags keeps working until 2027-01-01.
The icon choices of the edit panel are read from the view properties folder, view-properties since rename plan R2 (was property-view). No visible change.

The second column follows the page: it shows the page's object menu (navigation.context) or the root that holds the page's row, and is closed on a page that has neither; it no longer shows the root left open on another page. A root clicked in the first column is shown until a page is opened. Whether the column is open is kept once for the person, not per site.
navigation.load carries `page`, the page's path and query, and is asked again after a region swap; a host answers `context`, the object menu of that page, or leaves it out.
New setting first-answer: a server prints the first navigation.load answer in the menu's data-sf-settings island and the menu is drawn from it at once, without a skeleton; the port answers behind it.
The caption «Общее для всех сайтов» under a section of the install level is drawn only when the host offers the site switch (capabilities include site-switch). Nothing to change for a host.

sf-admin-menu-search.summary: 1.0 name of sf-admin-menu-query {kind: menu, query, requestId}; follows it until 2026-12-01.

sf-admin-menu-settings-reset.summary: 1.0 name of sf-admin-menu-reset {kind: settings, target, base_revision, baseRevision}; follows it until 2026-12-01.

sf-host-port-request.summary: Ask the page for a host port when connecting. A page that answers with simai.admin-navigation-port gets the navigation shell; a page that answers nothing gets the items menu, unchanged. Retired: the page hands the port with connectPort({port}); still sent until 2026-12-01.

sf-admin-menu-intent.summary: 1.0: what a person asked of the host. Since 1.2.0 each intent is told by its verb (sf-admin-menu-refresh, -open, -toggle, -save, -query, -create, -rename, -delete, -read, -reset, -sign-out: {kind, ..., intent, payload}); this name follows each until 2026-12-01.

intent.description: The port intent, e.g. navigation.load or favourite.add.

payload.description: The intent's payload as the port declares it.

setHostPort.summary: Bind the host of simai.admin-navigation-port; the menu then draws the navigation shell instead of the items menu.

returns.description: The outcome of connect-port, whose alias this is: {outcome: "applied"}, or refused with no-port, other-port or port-unsupported.

setRecentResults.summary: What the host offers an empty search field: a recent list, standing until it sets another. Deprecated: the setting recent-results (until 2026-12-01).

connectPort.summary: The Framework's base action connect-port {port} (standard 1.3.8 §4.1, §4.9): hands the navigation port, kept as sfPort; answers an outcome (refused other-port for another port, port-unsupported for a version the menu does not take). setHostPort is its alias.
